data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English word 'seo-gyfe,' meaning 'joy' or 'happiness.' In the Bible, the name Joyce is not directly attributed to any particular character, but the joyful spirit of God is felt throughout Scripture. The name Joyce carries the meaning “Joy, happiness” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Joyce usually hope their child will grow to embody joy, happiness and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.name: Τζόυς
in_greek.meaning: Χριστιανικό όνομα που σημαίνει χαρά ή ευτυχία
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Τζόυς προέρχεται από το χριστιανικό όνομα που σημαίνει χαρά ή ευτυχία. Είναι παράγωγο από το εβραϊκό όνομα 'שמחה' και από την ελληνική λέξη 'χάρη' (cháris), που σημαίνει χαρά ή απόλαυση. Το όνομα Τζόυς ήταν ευρέως διαδεδομένο κατά την βικτωριανή εποχή και θεωρήθηκε ως παραδοσιακό χριστιανικό όνομα.

historical_references.reference: Saint Joyce, also known as Saint Juventia, was a Christian martyr who lived during the late 3rd or early 4th century. She was the daughter of a Roman nobleman and converted to Christianity with her three sisters, Suosa, Vaca, and Vestina. They were all martyred together for refusing to sacrifice to Roman gods. Saint Joyce is the patron saint of travelers, especially those by water.

Another Saint Joyce is believed to have lived in the 15th century in Ireland. She was a nun and a member of the Benedictine Order. Legend has it that she was known for her great joy and generosity, and she was often called upon to intercede in times of famine or plague. Saint Joyce is also the patron saint of Ireland and is invoked for protection against storms at sea.
